articles.title: Why Does AI Cite Their Page and Not Yours? Diff Them With a Script
articles.excerpt: You've measured share of voice and found a prompt cluster where a competitor keeps getting recommended and cited, and you don't. The obvious next question is what's different about their page? Most pe…
articles.body: You've measured share of voice and found a prompt cluster where a competitor keeps getting recommended and cited, and you don't. The obvious next question is what's different about their page? Most people answer that by eyeballing two browser tabs. This post does it with a script: take the URLs AI engines cited for a prompt, fetch them the way a non-JavaScript crawler would, extract the features that tend to matter for extraction and citation, and print a diff against your page. It won't explain everything. Brand reputation and third-party mentions matter too, and they don't show up in page HTML. But it reliably catches the boring structural gaps, which are the fastest ones to fix.
articles.author: Furqan Khalid

articles.title: Copilot YOLO mode, dissected: what --yolo, /yolo and Allow all actually skip
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Copilot CLI: copilot --yolo (same flag as --allow-all), or /yolo in a running session. It is shorthand for --allow-all-tools + --allow-all-paths + --allow-all-urls. VS Code: pick Allow all in th…
articles.body: TL;DR Copilot CLI: copilot --yolo (same flag as --allow-all ), or /yolo in a running session. It is shorthand for --allow-all-tools + --allow-all-paths + --allow-all-urls . VS Code: pick Allow all in the chat permission picker, type /yolo , or set "chat.tools.global.autoApprove": true to make it permanent. What it skips: approval prompts. What it doesn't: your --deny-tool rules, and (in VS Code, explicitly documented) an enabled sandbox. Autopilot is a different switch. It keeps the agent iterating; YOLO approves its tool calls. Unattended runs usually want both. Everything here was checked on October 7, 2026 against GitHub's Copilot CLI reference, the github/copilot-cli changelog (1.0.93) and VS Code's agent docs in microsoft/vscode-docs.

articles.body: Originally published on tamiz.pro . Stop Flying Blind: Adding OpenTelemetry Tracing to Your AI Gateway Building an AI Gateway has become standard practice for organizations moving from experimental LLM playgrounds to production-grade applications. The gateway sits between your application code and multiple model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Local LLMs), handling routing, caching, rate limiting, and cost control. However, without deep observability, your team is essentially flying blind. When a user complains that the chat response was "slow" or "weird," can you distinguish between a network timeout, a specific model hallucination, or a cache miss that triggered a redundant expensive inference?

articles.body: This week QGIS merged QEP #387 : "No LLM, AI or agent assisted code contributions are allowed in the qgis/qgis repository." Violators face "code reversion and contributor rights sanctioning." It replaced a human-in-the-loop policy, it passed a vote, it is on master as of October 7. The HN thread is at three hundred comments and counting, split between "rationing attention is fair" and "this will age like milk." The line that settles the whole debate was written by the project itself, in the proposal's discussion. Asked how compliance will work, a core contributor answered: did you in good conscience write the code yourself. That is not an enforcement mechanism.

articles.title: Gemini CLI YOLO mode, read from the source: why settings.json can't turn it on
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Start YOLO with gemini --approval-mode=yolo, or press Ctrl+Y in a running session. --yolo / -y still work but are deprecated, and combining --yolo with --approval-mode is an error. You cannot ma…
articles.body: TL;DR Start YOLO with gemini --approval-mode=yolo , or press Ctrl+Y in a running session. --yolo / -y still work but are deprecated, and combining --yolo with --approval-mode is an error. You cannot make YOLO the default in settings.json . That's a deliberate design choice, and the code that enforces it is three lines long. YOLO only removes approval prompts. The sandbox (Seatbelt, Docker, Podman, gVisor, LXC) is a separate switch, and in the current source YOLO never turns it on. In an untrusted folder, any mode other than default gets forced back to default . If security.disableYoloMode or admin secure mode is set, asking for YOLO is a fatal config error, not a silent downgrade.

articles.title: The moon could turn astronauts into 'walking, high voltage capacitors' that accidentally zap spacecraft
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions.
articles.body: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions. The agency opened a "Lunar Grounding Challenge" to avoid situations where an astronaut on the moon could become "a walking, high voltage capacitor." Submissions for the $150,000 competition are due Jan. 15 and you can see the requirements here . NASA is hoping to put astronaut boots at the lunar south pole in 2028 during the Artemis 4 or 5 missions, on the first landing mission since NASA's Apollo 17 in 1972. But simulations suggest that both "tribocharging" (electric-charge transfer between two objects) and plasma charging (from ambient gas in the region) could build up electric charge on spacesuits.

articles.title: The 'Halloween Fireballs' are coming. Here's what to expect from the Taurids this year
articles.excerpt: The Southern and Northern Taurid meteor showers will produce occasional bright, slow-moving meteors worldwide during October and November, with moon-free peaks in 2026.
articles.body: They don't produce anything like the torrent of "shooting stars" associated with August's Perseids or December's Geminids, but the Taurid meteor showers have something else going for them — fireballs. The Taurids are famous for occasionally producing exceptionally bright, slow-moving meteors that can streak dramatically across the night sky from September to December. As a bonus, they're visible from both the Northern and Southern hemispheres. That's because they appear to emanate from the constellation Taurus, which sits close to the ecliptic, the apparent path the sun takes across the sky as Earth orbits around it. The Taurids are actually two closely related showers — the Southern Taurids and Northern Taurids — whose activity overlaps in late October and November.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 12, 1964: The Soviet Union launches Voskhod 1, the 1st multi-person cosmonaut crew, into space
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched Voskhod 1, a 24-hour crewed mission that achieved several "firsts" for human spaceflight. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched Voskhod 1, a 24-hour crewed mission that achieved several "firsts" for human spaceflight . This was the first time that a spacecraft carried more than one person into orbit, with three cosmonauts packed inside the spacecraft. Only two cosmonauts were originally supposed to fly on this mission, but Soviet politicians pressured the Russian space program to add one more. This left no room for spacesuits on board, so this also became the first spaceflight without spacesuits . Two of the crewmembers, an engineer and a doctor, became the first civilians to go to space. On Oct. 12, 1964, the Soviet Union launched the first multiperson mission, Voskhod 1, which launched three Russian cosmonauts into space.

articles.title: Namibian salt flats look like an alien planet | Space photo of the day for Oct. 12, 2026
articles.excerpt: The Etosha Pan in northern Namibia, the largest salt flat in the country, looks otherworldly in this satellite photo.
articles.body: The Etosha Pan, Namibia's largest salt pan, seen from space. (Image credit: Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026), processed by ESA) A neon blue pool swirls amongst what look like clouds, all surrounded by a bright red stretch of land. This might look like the surface of an alien planet , but it's actually a salt flat right here on Earth , seen from space. What is it? Etosha National Park in northern Namibia hosts the largest salt pan, or piece of land covered with salt and other minerals, in the country. This image of the Etosha Pan was captured on April 5 of this year by Europe's Copernicus Sentinel-2 mission, which consists of two identical satellites in the same orbit.

articles.body: "Tomb Raider" celebrates its 30th anniversary this month. Coming off the back of the hugely successful "Tomb Raider 2", developer Core Design had big plans for the third entry, including kayaking, those iconic London levels, and, of course, a level featuring a UFO in Area 51. Although it looked small on the outside, the UFO featured multiple floors for players to explore as they searched for a vital artifact, all as enemies swarmed in.

articles.title: What caused a mysterious atmospheric explosion in Siberia in 1908?
articles.excerpt: Fire erupted in the morning skies over Siberia on June 30, 1908, as an atmospheric explosion occurred that remains unmatched by any similar event in modern history.
articles.body: Fire erupted in the morning skies over Siberia on June 30, 1908, as an atmospheric explosion occurred that remains unmatched by any similar event in modern history. That day, at approximately 7:15 a.m. local time, observers in Siberia's remote Tunguska region became witnesses to the entry of a brilliant fireball into Earth's atmosphere , trailing smoke across the dawn sky and culminating in a flash brighter than the sun itself. Within seconds, the explosion and resulting shock waves that followed reportedly knocked some members of the nearby Indigenous Evenki population off their feet, and caused damage to dwellings and livestock, while seismic instruments hundreds of miles away logged tremors caused by the blast.
